title: IMD forecasts heavy to very heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Sub Himalayan West Bengal & Sikkim - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Bihar, Sub Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim today.

Heavy rainfall is also expected over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh and Jharkhand till tomorrow. Similar conditions are expected over Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and North-Eastern parts of India today.

The Weather Department has also forecast thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep, North Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands till tomorrow.

title: IMD predicts extremely heavy rainfall over Assam and Meghalaya tomorrow - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Assam and Meghalaya for tomorrow. Heavy rainfall is also expected over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, and parts of North East India during the next two days. Similar weather conditions are expected over Kerala, Mahe, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Uttar Pradesh during the next two to three days.

The Met Department also predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Jammu-Kashmir, Andhra Pradesh, Karaikal, Karnataka, Jharkhand, Odisha, and Andaman and Nicobar Islands tomorrow.

Meanwhile parts of Delhi witnessed rainfall today. The IMD predicted a generally cloudy sky with a spell of moderate rain at a few places of the national capital during early morning tomorrow. According to the Weather Agency, the maximum temperature will be around 32 to 34 degrees Celsius in Delhi while the minimum temperature will hover around 23 to 25 degrees Celsius tomorrow.

title: Uttarakhand: लगातार बारिश से कई जगह बाढ़ और भूस्खलन के हालात, हाई अलर्ट पर प्रशासन - totaltv.in
article_text:
Uttarakhand: उत्तराखंड में लगातार हो रही बारिश के कारण कई नदियों का स्तर बढ़ने से कुछ जिलों में बाढ़ और भूस्खलन के हालात बन गए हैं। इसे देखते हुए राज्य भर में अधिकारी हाई अलर्ट पर हैं। रुद्रप्रयाग में रात भर हुई बारिश के बाद अलकनंदा नदी खतरे के निशान से ऊपर बह रही है। निचले इलाकों के कई घरों में बाढ़ का पानी आ गया है, जबकि सुविधानगर में एक नाले पर बना पुल पूरा पानी में डूब गया है। Uttarakhand
केदारनाथ रूट पर तिलवाड़ा के पास भारी बारिश से नेशनल हाईवे मलबे और बड़े पत्थरों के कारण बंद है। वहां खड़ी कई गाड़ियों को भी नुकसान पहुंचा है। अधिकारियों ने राहत काम शुरू कर दिया है और लोगों से सावधानी बरतने की अपील की है। देहरादून में लगातार बारिश की वजह से टपकेश्वर महादेव मंदिर के पास तमसा नदी का स्तर लगातार बढ़ रहा है। Uttarakhand
एहतियातन, गुरुवार को सभी स्कूलों को बंद रखने का आदेश दिया गया। हरिद्वार में बुधवार देर रात तेज बारिश के कारण कई जगहों पर पानी भर गया, जिससे आम जनजीवन प्रभावित हुआ है, लोगों का जरूरी काम से आना-जाना तक मुश्किल हो गया। Uttarakhand
मौसम विभाग ने देहरादून, चमोली और बागेश्वर जिलों में ‘ऑरेंज एलर्ट’ जारी किया है, जबकि उत्तराखंड के बाकी हिस्सों के लिए ‘येलो एलर्ट’ लागू है। अधिकारियों ने स्थानीय लोगों और सैलानियों से अपील की है कि वे मौसम संबंधी चेतावनियों को गंभीरता से लें और बेवजह यात्रा करने से बचें। Uttarakhand

title: IMD warns of heavy rain, thunderstorms in J&K - Brighter Kashmir
article_text:
New Delhi, Aug 5: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast widespread rainfall with thunderstorms, lightning, and heavy rain over large parts of northwest India, including Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-Baltistan-Muzaffarabad, and Uttarakhand in the coming days.
According to the IMD’s All India Weather Summary and Forecast Bulletin issued Wednesday morning, fairly widespread to widespread rainfall is likely over Himachal Pradesh, Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-Baltistan-Muzaffarabad, and Uttarakhand during August 5-11, with isolated thunderstorms and lightning. Similar rainfall is expected over Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi, and Punjab during August 5-6.

The remaining parts of northwest India are likely to see isolated to scattered rainfall. Isolated heavy rainfall over Jammu-Kashmir-Ladakh-Gilgit-Baltistan-Muzaffarabad on August 5 and during August 9-11.

Himachal Pradesh is likely to receive isolated heavy rainfall during August 5-11, while Haryana, Chandigarh, Delhi and Punjab are likely to witness isolated heavy rainfall during August 5-6. For Uttarakhand, isolated thunderstorms and lightning are likely during August 5-11. Isolated heavy rainfall is forecast during August 6-11.

According to an official of MeT Kashmir, during past 24 hours significant rainfall was recorded in Jammu region with Udhampur receiving 66.6 mm rainfall, Kathua 81 mm, Samba 47 mm & Katra 51 mm respectively.

“From August 6-8, there is a possibility of light to moderate rain/ thundershower at many places with brief intense showers at few places,” he said.
“From August 9-11, there is a possibility of a few spells of light to moderate rain/thundershower at most places with heavy rainfall/brief intense heavy showers at few districts,” the MeT official said. “From August 12-15, there is a possibility of light rain/thunderstorms at many places with brief intense showers at few places.”

The MeT has warned of heavy rain, brief intense heavy showers at few districts during 5th Aug & 9-11th August.

It also warned that torrential rain, brief intense heavy showers may generate flashfloods, landslides at vulnerable places.

title: IMD predicts severe heatwave conditions over North, West India; heavy rainfall in NE region - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heat wave to severe heat wave conditions over West Madhya Pradesh and West Rajasthan for the next two days. East Rajasthan, Gujarat and Maharashtra are expected to reel under heat wave conditions tomorrow. The Weather agency also predicted heavy to very heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam and Meghalaya tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy rainfall is also likely over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Kerala, Mahe, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, Sub Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal during the next three days. Places over Delhi, Punjab, Haryana, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Chandigarh, Odisha, West Bengal and the Northeastern states are expected to experience thunderstorms and lightning tomorrow. According to the Met department, thundersquall conditions are expected during the next 2 days over Jharkhand, Coastal Karnataka, and North Interior Karnataka.

IMD further said that conditions are becoming favourable for the advance of southwest monsoon over parts of south Bay of Bengal, Andaman Sea and Andaman and Nicobar Islands around Saturday.
